draft.briefing: Hey, you're at Palakkad Fort! Hyder Ali captured and rebuilt this fort in 1766, and its sturdy battlements and moat are still right here in the heart of the city.
draft.hungryLine: Palakkad leans vegetarian, thanks to its Tamil Brahmin culture. Look for kalan, a dish unique to Palakkad, or dosa, idli and vada.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Palakkad Fort is a 1 min walk, and the Hanuman Temple on its grounds is 2 min. Martyr's Monument is about 6 min on foot.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Walk out to the paddy fields at Azhchapparamba Junction on Thrissur Road.
moodReplies.surprise-me: The fort changed hands fast. Hyder Ali rebuilt it in 1766, and by 1784 it had fallen to the Zamorin.

legends.title: The river of yagas
legends.body: It is said that in ancient times, yagas were performed on the banks of the Shokanasini, another name for the Bharathapuzha. So the area became Yaga-kara, which later turned into Yakkara.

legends.title: Konganpada
legends.body: Every year, usually in March, Chittur's Konganpada remembers the victory of the Chittur Nairs over the Konganadu militia in 918 AD. At night, men in buffalo-head masks stage mock fights.

tips.title: Come in mid-November.
tips.body: Kalpathy Rathotsavam lights up the village streets with a procession of temple chariots.

tips.title: Use the Stadium Bus Stand.
tips.body: It's the biggest private bus stand in Palakkad, with restaurants and shops close by.

story.title: Hyder Ali's fort
story.body: Hyder Ali captured the fort and rebuilt it in 1766. In 1784 it fell into the hands of the Zamorin.

story.title: A municipality
story.body: Under British rule the town, then called Palghat, became a municipality on 1 November 1866. It was part of the South Malabar region of Malabar District.

story.title: A district of its own
story.body: Palakkad district was carved out of the old Malabar District on 1 January 1957. The same year, the music academy that became Chembai Memorial Government Music College opened.

story.title: Cricket at the fort
story.body: Fort Maidan was a local cricket ground until 2002. The Ranji Trophy arrived in 2003, and it's now a regular first-class venue.

story.title: Tipu's Fort
story.body: Many still call it Tipu's Fort. It sits in the heart of the city, with a Hanuman temple inside its grounds.
